ranking_note: Authored from the before descriptions at commit fd862a49b848e143ec31bebc054c01d31150a26a, frozen before the rewrite; protocol per /playbooks:skill-authoring ## Measurement. Competitors are improvement:improve (ships one fix as one PR, where find only ranks and never edits), architecture:improve (module-level friction only), code-tidying:tidy (one structure-only tidying PR), codebase-health:audit (doc, config and code drift), review:fanout (breadth review of one change), work-items:scan-todos (TODO and FIXME markers) and performance:go-faster (speed of the development process). find owns the cross-dimension, evidence-cited, sized ranking of what is worth improving.

queries.request: Look over this repo and tell me where our time would be best spent next, ranked, with evidence for each item.
I want a list of improvement opportunities for the checkout service, each sized small, medium or large. Don't change anything yet.
Where's the biggest payoff in this project right now? Code, config, our Claude setup, whatever.
Do a tech-debt pass over the billing module and rank what's worth tackling.
Run an unattended sweep tonight and file work items for the best candidates you find.
What are the top things we could make better in the API layer? Back each one with something you actually measured or read.
Give me a prioritized backlog of upgrades for this repo across product, performance and tooling.
Which changes would matter most for the reporting feature? Only the large ones please.
Scan the ingestion pipeline for things worth fixing and tell me which ones we can't judge yet because nothing measures them.
This retry helper is ugly. Clean it up and open a small PR for it.
Bring the logging setup in Program.cs up to current .NET guidance and send me the PR.
Find the shallow modules in our services and walk me through redesigning the worst interface.
Check whether our README and config still match what the code actually does.
Run every reviewer over this branch and merge their findings into one report.
Pick one small piece of code and fix it right now, no need to show me a list.
Go through the source and deal with every FIXME and HACK comment.
Do a quick boy-scout pass on the parser: guard clauses, extracted helpers, one structure-only PR.
Our sessions feel sluggish. What in our hooks and git workflow is slowing us down?
